title: Maple and Percy's Map Mishap
markdown:
Maple the rabbit liked things just so. Carrots stood in crunch-order. Pebbles twinkled in a tidy ring. The burrow smelled of dried leaves and neat cushions.

WHOOSH. Percy the parrot landed on Maple’s nose, a rainbow blur with a dewdrop in his beak.

“Super shiny,” Percy said.

Maple liked quiet. Percy liked loud. Maple liked order. Percy liked everything that glittered, giggled, or zoomed. They were the bestest friends all the same.

Percy tugged a crinkly paper from a dusty box. Wiggly lines. A fat red X.

“A treasure map,” he screeched. “My uncle’s hamster’s goldfish’s third cousin said there’s treasure.”

Maple’s nose twitched. Treasure might be shiny. Treasure might also be messy.

“A plan is needed,” Maple said.

“Plan schman,” Percy said. “Let’s go.”

Maple’s ears drooped a fraction. “What if we get lost? What if it is all crumbs and puddles?”

Percy nudged him. “I’ll be your eyes. You be my clever planner.”

Maple packed very, very important snacks. Then he clutched the map, Percy rode his shoulder, and they zoomed into the Whispering Woods, where tall trees rustled like secrets telling jokes.

“The map says that way, past the grumpy rock,” Maple said.

Percy shrieked at a funny mushroom. He pointed at a shiny beetle. His chirps also found bright berries and the loudest, happiest frog song, which Maple wrote down, in his head, as Extra Snack Data.

First came the Giggling Stream, too wide to hop.

Maple paced. “Tricky.”

Percy dropped a bright feather. “A bridge.”

Maple stepped. WHOOSH. The feather was slicker than a banana peel. Splash. They tumbled into chuckling water, snacks bobbing like little boats.

They shook off, still laughing, and hurried on. Sleepy sunflowers nodded so hard the field spun. Maple’s whiskers drooped. Percy steered him by the ear until the ground stopped waltzing.

Then the Tickle-Bush Thicket grabbed. Prickly branches. Teeheehee from Percy’s feathers. Maple parted the twigs with careful paws, nose twitching, planner-mode on.

At last a twisty oak looked like the map. Maple frowned at the bark.

“Where is the X?”

Percy tilted his head. “Wait. It’s upside down. The X is here.” He tapped a knot that looked like a squished letter.

Oh, beak-grabs. Percy had held the map the wrong way up.

The sun dipped. Orange. Purple. Long shadows. Maple’s tidy thoughts jumbled like spilled carrots.

“We’re so far from home,” he whispered.

He slumped on a mossy log. The paper was a damp mess. They were tired. They were hungry. The burrow felt a million miles away.

Percy went quiet, which almost never happened, and nuzzled Maple’s warm fur.

“I’ll be your eyes,” Percy said, smaller this time. “You be my clever planner.”

The woods still felt huge. Maple still felt small. With Percy beside him, the shadows did not quite win.

Maple’s whiskers wiggled. “Past the three twisty trees is a shortcut. I remember.”

Percy chirped. “Shiny.” A familiar pebble lay in the moss, one of his shinies, dropped earlier, right by the turning.

They followed Maple’s memory and Percy’s lucky pebble. The burrow glowed in the last sunlight. They tumbled in, giggling. The map flopped by the door, X still slightly squashed.

They shared the juicy berry Maple had saved. Maple even tidied a stray feather Percy had dropped, setting it in the pebble ring as if it had always belonged.

“Best adventure ever,” Percy said, then yawned a giant parrot yawn.

Snuggled among neat cushions and dried-leaf smell, they drifted off, dreaming of sparkly things and giggling water, and of the next outing — with the map the right way up.
